message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on the current auction.

The auction is for NORTH_CAROLINA_AVENUE. The current bid is $107 and I have $726 cash. I will bid up to about $150, the mortgage value, then drop out if p4 continues. Winning at or below that amount lets me mortgage the property back for net cash and deny p4 a second green.

I will bid $108. That keeps me under the $150 cap.

Bidding $108 nets $42 cash after mortgaging. Denying p4 a second green is valuable because they already hold Pennsylvania Avenue and cannot complete the set without trading with p1. Their light blue monopoly with four houses each is also dangerous.

I am checking the board order to see how many rolls it takes to reach the dark blues from Pennsylvania Avenue.

I have mapped the standard Monopoly board order. I am currently on Pennsylvania Avenue.

I am checking the rent values for the dark blues ahead. Park Place with three houses costs $1100 and Boardwalk with four costs $1700. I only have $726 cash, so I cannot afford either without selling houses. My pink monopoly of St Charles, States, and Virginia has four houses on each property.

Selling all twelve houses from the pink monopoly yields $600. Adding that to my cash gives $1326. Mortgaging the three properties adds another $220, for a total of $1546. That is still short of the $1700 rent on Boardwalk. I am bankrupt if I land there without more assets.

I have a get out of jail card but no cash. Spending $108 on the auction leaves me with $618 cash, which combined with house sales gives $1218 total. That covers Park Place at $1100 with $118 left over. Without the auction bid I would have $1326 total, still short of Boardwalk but able to pay Park Place. The extra $108 improves my margin against Park Place but does not change my inability to survive Boardwalk.

Bidding exactly $150 would leave me with a mortgaged property worth $150 but costing $165 to unmortgage, so it is slightly negative. Bidding above that would lose money on the round-trip and reduce my survival cash. I am currently past the light blue properties, which are dangerous to me only if I circle around.

p4 is in jail with $763 cash. They cannot pay rent on the dark blues ahead. Denying them North Carolina Avenue removes their leverage to complete the green set.

p4's cash is being bled while they remain in jail. They cannot pay rent on the dark blues ahead, so staying in jail is strategically sound for them late in the game. I am now calculating the rent for my pink monopoly with four houses.

Four houses on the pink monopoly yield $625, $625, and $700 in rent. That is solid but not lethal like the dark blues.

p1 is currently on NORTH_CAROLINA_AVENUE with only $29 cash. They declined to buy the property because it was unowned, so the auction started immediately.

p1 also holds Marvin Gardens with one house, plus Atlantic and Ventnor unmortgaged.

p1 owns the full yellow set with one house on Marvin Gardens. They are cash poor but property rich.

From Pennsylvania Avenue, Park Place is three spaces away and Boardwalk is five. The probability of landing on either next roll is two in thirty-six.
